newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian airlines to lease 38 planes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russian airlines to lease 38 planes in 1997.

text.p: Russian airlines plan to lease 38 new Russian-built passenger aircraft worth a total four trillion roubles in 1997, a senior Russian Federal Aviation Service (FAS) official said on Friday.

Viktor Samokhin, head of technical department, told Reuters that Russia's eight aviation leasing companies did not have the money to buy the planes, but hoped to receive government guarantees for four trillion roubles to do so.
One of the conditions of these guarantees is that the leasing companies form a national association.
"These companies or airlines have no funds to lease or buy new aircraft and the crisis will be resolved after a national leasing system is set up in Russia," Samokhin said.
Samokhin did not have information about plans to lease Western-built aircraft, but noted that only Aeroflot and Transaero had the right to lease foreign planes.

Alexander Smolko, Aeroflot-Leasing vice-president, said Russian plane-makers would not be able to produce 38 planes this year because in recent years they have lost skilled staff and links between companies in the industry have been broken.
"The industry is in deep crisis now...and I do not see light at the end of the tunnel," he said.

Eduard Neimark, head of the aviation industry department of the defence industry ministry, said recently that Russian carriers had planned to buy or lease 80 new passenger and cargo planes last year, but only received about 25 planes and helicopters, compared with 83 aircraft in 1992.
Russian civil airlines needed 138 new aircraft for 1997, he said.
Samokhin said that during the last three years Russian carriers had withdrawn from service 500 planes and helicopters a year.
"FAS experts said carriers will need 441 aircraft and 211 helicopters by 2001 to replace their old fleet," he said.
